title: Enterprise residency request flow and risk-adjusted prioritization
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Purpose: define a repeatable intake->triage->routing playbook for enterprise region/residency requests that balances legal constraints, customer revenue, and operational cost/risk. This doc formalizes: 1) an intake form and minimum artifacts for fast adjudication, 2) a risk-adjusted scoring rubric for prioritization, 3) automated routing outputs (approve/deny/soft-residency/adjacent-failover) and 4) required engineering deliverables for each outcome. Scope excludes ad-hoc infra-only requests and pure capacity increases without residency constraints.

Why this ticket: we continue to get high-touch enterprise requests that require both rapid decisioning and clear SLAs for failover. Current ad-hoc decisions create engineering churn and inconsistent customer expectations. This playbook will reduce time-to-decision, create a consistent handoff to Eng/Sales/Legal, and produce measurable metrics for pipeline prioritization.

Key trade-offs considered: 
- Speed vs auditability: a lightweight intake speeds approvals but risks insufficient evidence for compliance; mitigation: require a minimal legal attestation plus optional full-data-flow diagram for high-risk geographies.
- Rehost vs soft-residency: fully-hosted regional deployment has higher cost/time; soft-residency (data tokenization or pseudonymization with audit logs) may meet many customers' needs faster but not all legal regimes.
- Failover semantics: prefer local-region replica when available to minimize latency; if not possible, use adjacent-region failover with documented privacy mitigations.

Outcome desired: a triage flow and scoring sheet that outputs one of (1) Approved — regional hosting scheduled, (2) Approved with mitigations — soft-residency or PS-proxy pattern allowed, (3) Defer — needs more artifacts, (4) Deny — incompatible with residency requirements. Each outcome must map to a set of engineering tickets and a timeline estimate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form template exists in Confluence and Drive. 2) Scoring rubric computed as actual numeric score in a spreadsheet and validated against at least 5 historical requests. 3) Triage runbook and playbook published to Confluence with clear owner per decision outcome. 4) Handoff checklist produces ENG ticket template and legal review checklist. 5) Pilot the flow on 3 active enterprise requests and record time-to-decision <= 7 business days.
triage_steps: 1. Intake: collector fills ‘Residency Intake Form’ (link in artifacts). 2. Initial PM review within 2 business days; flag high-legal risk for Legal & Security. 3. Run scoring rubric and produce recommended action. 4. Convene triage meeting for scores in the gray zone (scores 40-60). 5. Produce decision + required ENG deliverables and SLA. 6. Track outcome in region-requests dashboard and update customer-facing timeline.
scoring_rubric: We propose a 100-point risk-adjusted rubric with weighted buckets: Legal/regulatory (30), Revenue (deal ARR & strategic importance) (25), Tech lift / infra complexity (20), Capacity/regional availability (15), Fallback complexity & operational burden (10). Example thresholds: >=75 auto-approve to scheduling; 50-74 require PM+Legal signoff and SRE capacity check; <=49 deprioritize or require alternative mitigations. We will maintain the rubric as a Google Sheet with links to evidence and automated score calculations.
stakeholders: Engineering: Eng lead assigned per request
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket, 2 weeks): publish intake template, scoring sheet, and runbook; implement intake form (Forms -> Sheets) and notification Slack #geo-triage. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Template ENG tickets and automated label sync with Linear; SRE runbook for capacity checks. Phase 3 (4-8 weeks): implement light automation to populate scorecard from intake and link to a decision Slack thread + create CICD guardrails for approved regional builds. Each phase produces clear owner, checklist, and playbook doc.
rollout_notes: Pilot to 3 prioritized accounts (identified by Sales) for two-week pilot. Capture decision latency, number of evidence items requested, and rework cycles. After pilot, iterate rubric weights based on observed outcomes and stakeholder feedback. Communicate new SLA windows to Sales and Solutions. Update public-facing entitlement docs after internal sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-scored requests causing downstream audit exposure. Mitigation: any request with legal/regulatory score >= 20 must have Legal review checkpoint. Risk: SRE capacity shortfall for multi-region buildouts. Mitigation: require SRE capacity sign-off and offer adjacent-region failover as interim. Risk: customer dissatisfaction with soft-residency. Mitigation: enable a clear path to full residency with cost/time expectations documented.
metrics_to_track:
- Time to first decision (days)
- Percent of requests approved vs denied
- Number of follow-up evidence requests per intake
- Engineering effort (story points) per approval
- Customer satisfaction (post-decision survey)
- Compliance exceptions created
